doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Earning more per concert in France and Japan
summary: She makes more abroad, getting twice as much for one concert and about 75 percent more overall.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Just in conjunction with that question, and this is rather personal, so you don‘t have to give me figures, but just so we have some idea, what percentage, would you say, of your income is made in the United States, and what percentage is made outside of the United States?

Well, let‘s see. When I was doing those three years, we were everywhere but home. I made a lot more money. Well, it‘s especially good right now in . . . okay, I‘m sorry. Since I‘m well known in France, I make a lot of money in France and Japan, and you don‘t have to work yourself to death. Like you go over there and you do one show, right, and they don‘t call them shows; they call them concerts. You do one concert. You‘re going to get twice as much money for that one concert. Here, Chicago wants me to come in and do something, and I said, ―No concert, right?‖ Yeah, they want me hooked up with some ladies, women in jazz business. I said, ―I‘m going to do one. If they want one, okay, then I cancel.‖ You know what I mean, because they‘re going to take me through a whole bunch of changes. But 75 percent more money than, you know, I make here. They don‘t work your ass off either.
